clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old female with a history of excessive alcohol consumption (1 bottle of vodka per day) presented to the ED with dizziness, unsteady gait, and recurrent falls over an extended period, resulting in two prior hospital admissions within 6 months. On neurological examination, she demonstrated an ataxic gait without weakness and dysdiadochokinesis in the right hand, indicating cerebellar dysfunction. Laboratory studies revealed anemia, hypokalaemia, hypomagnesemia, and elevated inflammatory markers consistent with chronic alcohol use and nutritional deficiency. MRI brain imaging demonstrated demyelination involving the splenium of the corpus callosum with marked cerebellar atrophy. These findings were reviewed in a neuro-radiology meeting and concluded to be consistent with Marchiafava-Bignami disease. Treatment was initiated with vitamin B supplementation, alcohol cessation counseling, and referral to rehabilitation for physiotherapy with graded exercises aimed at improving mobility.
